gaps.explanation: All seven governmental fund columns of the GAAP Statement of Revenues, Expenditures and Changes in Fund Balances (pp7, 9) are in detail[], but from the Budget and Actual (Budget Basis) schedules (pp13-19). GAAP total revenues (pp7, 9) vs budget-basis totals: General 28,063,912 vs 27,392,667 (p13) +671,245; Debt Service 5,450,556 vs 5,100,072 (p16) +350,484; Keno 1,499,615 vs 1,533,947 (p14) -34,332; Capital Improvements 97,461 vs 97,460 (p17) +1; Economic Development 226,557 vs 226,557 (p18) 0; 84th Street Redevelopment 3,986,886 vs 3,562,663 (p19) +424,223 (the GAAP column counts Intergovernmental 77,836 as revenue, the budget schedule prints it as Federal Grant under other financing sources); Police Academy 263,070 vs 271,075 (p15) -8,005. Sum = 1,403,616 = gap; statement 39,588,057 (p9) vs schedules 38,184,441. No fix.

GAAP total expenditures (pp8, 9) vs budget-basis schedule totals: General 25,000,247 vs 24,967,275 (p13); Debt Service 4,773,492 vs 4,697,022 (p16); Keno 781,925 vs 806,942 (p14); Capital Improvements 6,352,789 vs 5,559,814 (p17); Economic Development 1,154,825 vs 1,154,825 (p18); 84th Street 5,263,281 vs 7,112,702 (p19); Police Academy 215,939 vs 207,311 (p15). Statement 43,542,498 (p9); schedule lines 44,505,890 (printed budget totals 44,505,891, 1 of rounding inside the schedules). Schedule above by 963,392 only from the budget vs GAAP basis. No fix.

Statement Total Governmental Funds prints Transfers, net (726) (p9; GAAP fund columns pp8-9: General (268,317), Debt Service (11,129,537), Keno (323,183), Capital Improvements 10,713,737, Economic Development 1,006,574, net (726)). Detail records the budget-basis transfers gross per fund: General (1,731) p13, Keno (323,183) p14, Debt Service (11,129,537) p16 = 11,454,451 out; Capital Improvement +9,862,602 p17, Economic Development +1,006,574 p18 in. The difference is gross-vs-net plus the budget-basis General (1,731 vs 268,317) and Capital Improvement (9,862,602 vs 10,713,737) transfer amounts. No fix.
